applied.name: hexanedinitrile
applied.value: Primary ThermoML observation confirmed at 298.15 K: eps=32.12 +/- 0.1, pure component, zero frequency, dataset 3, DOI 10.1021/je300958c. ECW-308 Table S3 lists this compound with a value of 30.00 at 25 C citing Duncan, Salem & Abu-Lebdeh, J. Electrochem. Soc. 2013, 160, A838 (DOI 10.1149/2.088306jes). That cited table was retrieved on 2026-09-24 from the NRC Publications Archive accepted manuscript (record 431ad01c-3fb7-4610-923b-99d08c6a4c16): Table I on p. A840 reports the compound as eps=30, not 30.00, so the two decimals in ECW-308 are unsupported precision rather than a second measurement. The paper records that dielectric constants were measured with a Brookhaven BI-870 meter, but Table I carries no per-row provenance, temperature, frequency or uncertainty, so the value cannot be promoted to a same-condition primary cross-check. It sits about 6.6% below the retained primary observation and is recorded as a source disagreement rather than an error. The values were not averaged.
applied.rationale: Appendix J requires a conflict record against the retained primary value, and now that the cited original table has been retrieved the record must state what that source actually reports instead of saying it was not retrieved.

applied.name: 2,5,8-trioxanonane
applied.value: Critical-compilation record: the stored value 7.3815 is the arithmetic mean of two pure-component zero-frequency ThermoML observations that agree within their uncertainties, 7.363 +/- 0.147 at 298.15 K (DOI 10.1016/j.jct.2008.09.006, dataset 7) and 7.4 +/- 0.15 at 298.15 K (DOI 10.1016/j.jct.2010.09.008, dataset 5). Both source DOIs are recorded in source_dois_all. ECW-308 Table S3 entry 96 (PDF p.74 / S73, DOI 10.1002/adfm.202212342) lists 7.40 at 25 C from a secondary compilation citing Huang et al., Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1808393. This agrees with the 2010 ThermoML observation; the stored value remains the mean of the two zero-frequency primary observations, and the secondary value was not averaged in. Source-tier check, 2026-09-24: the cited work (DOI 10.1002/adma.201808393) was checked through OpenAlex, Unpaywall, Europe PMC and PubMed and is a closed-access review rather than an original measurement, so the ECW-308 entry is a third-hand relay and is retained only as a consistency check.
applied.rationale: Appendix J source-tier discipline: record that the compilation's own citation is a review so the value is not mistaken for a measurement.

applied.name: vinylene carbonate
applied.value: Conflict record: the stored 126 at 298 K comes from an open-access article text (10.1002/cssc.202402091) and is reproduced by the ECW-308 compilation (10.1002/adfm.202212342 Table S3, 126.00 at 25 C). Following ECW-308's citation [3] to Hall et al., J. Electrochem. Soc. 2018, 165, A2365 (DOI 10.1149/2.1351810jes, CC BY 4.0), Table I of that open-access paper lists vinylene carbonate as eps=126 and attributes it to Saadi & Lee, J. Chem. Soc. B 1966, 5-6 (DOI 10.1039/j29660000005). The abstract of the 1966 paper states that the dielectric constant and dipole moment of vinylene carbonate have been measured, so a primary measurement source has now been identified; the two-page full text is paywalled, so the numeric value could not be read directly and no promotion to primary is claimed. The row stays conflict_open because a Knovel Critical Tables-derived interval of 78-127 disagrees. Vinylene carbonate melts near 295 K, so the 298 K observation sits close to the melting point.
applied.rationale: Appendix J requires the VC row to record what is actually known. The previous text claimed no primary measurement had been found, which the 2026-09-24 citation trace disproved.
